doc.title: Mona Hinton interviewed by Milt Fillius and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995

title: Filming the Esquire photograph of the musicians
summary: Mona shot the only movie footage at the Esquire group photo session while Milt took stills.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Now tell me about the picture that is now making the rounds, of all the musicians, that you gave me a copy of that picture some years ago, and now it’s in a movie and you’re mentioned as being one of the photographers. Can you tell us about that?
Yes. Esquire wanted that picture, I think it was 1956 or 1958 —

57? Well anyway, they had asked all the musicians, contacted lots of musicians who were in New York and asked them to come to this particular address in front of the brownstone to get this picture for Esquire magazine. And Milton had two still cameras, he was shoot, shoot, shooting away, and he had a little eight millimeter movie camera, and he asked me, he gave it to me and said, you know take some footage while the musicians are greeting each other. So that’s what I did. And it just so happened that that was the only movie film that was taken that day. So it was very important because they had so many stills, but this way it allowed them to animate the still pictures, and so it was very important. So that’s how I happened to get in on that.
It’s a marvelous picture. Mike have you seen that picture? Would you like to ask Mona a question?
